text:
ana: Quick note from today's bring-up: rkr-v2-int8 shows NDCG ~same but MRR top1 drops concentrated on docs that include small markdown tables.
marc: Any tiny repro?ui: Example from holdout:
query: "postgres bulk insert performance"
docA (fp16 top1): "Use COPY for bulk inserts.
| rows | time |
|---|---|
| 1k | 0.2s |
Sample output and perf notes."
docB (ptq bumped down): "Bulk loading: use COPY. See sample timings below.
|rows|time|
|1000|0.2s|
Notes on buffer tuning."
ana: Under ptq docB falls behind docA despite both being semantically similar. Token counts differ: fp16 docB tokens 58, int8 docB tokens 53.
marc: Token collapse around pipes and table cells? That could shift attention context windows and change top scoring.
rui: I ran tokenizer-diff: several merges like '|1000|0.2s|' becoming a single token in int8 pipeline. Seems packaging used a slightly different tokenizer config during quantization.
runbot: :robot_face: queued job 5181234567-token-diff: ./tools/tokenizer_diff --model rkr-v2-int8 --slice tables --samples 800
ana: Interim workaround: normalize tables to add spaces around pipes before tokenization. Quick eval with 1k samples: ptq+table-norm recovered ~2.6% MRR of the drop (total drop was ~3.9%).
oliver: That suggests preproc helps but not full parity. Next steps: 1) pin tokenizer sha in the build and fail packaging if mismatch; 2) run per-head calibration to see if specific attention heads responsible for table delimiters suffer; 3) add a small golden slice of table-heavy docs to onboarding CI.
marc: Agreed. I'll open PR to pin tokenizer config and add token-diff check. rui can you curate the table slice (500 items) and add to CI?
rui: Will do. I'll also dump head-wise activations for the top 20 mismatches and upload to the issue.
runbot: :white_check_mark: job 5181234567-token-diff completed: found 24 mismatches. Report: https://redwood.internal/tdiff/5181234567
ana: Thanks everyone. Once PRs land we'll rerun full holdout and close the loop.
